analysis.title: Healthcare: An AI antidote?
key_insights: Early, unofficial midterm results point to a Democratic sweep of both chambers. A veto from President Trump would limit major legislative change without bipartisan support. Pictet sees the policy backdrop as potentially more supportive for providers, while drugmakers stay exposed to pricing and Medicare-related pressure.
US Health Care's relative performance against the S&P 500 has reached its highest level of the year, breaking above the summer highs and the February peak. Recovery began from the June low.
European Health Care has rebounded sharply against the STOXX Europe 600 since September and recovered much of its 2026 decline. Relative performance is still below the February peak.

XLV/SPY has broken above its multi-year downtrend and reclaimed its key moving averages. RSI is 72.5, which Pictet calls stretched near term. Holding above the 0.2323 breakout area would support further outperformance.

Year to date, equal-weight Health Care (RSPH) is up 25.3%, cap-weighted XLV is up 20.2% and the S&P 500 is up 10.9%. Since 6 October, XLV is up 10.5%, RSPH up 7.9% and SPY down 3.5%, so the latest leg is more concentrated.
Eli Lilly rose about 11% over the week after stronger-than-expected earnings and lifted XLV to a new all-time high. Lilly is now roughly 16% of XLV.
Breadth remains strong: 86.7% of US Health Care constituents are above their 50-day moving average and 88.3% are above their 200-day.

On 30 October the S&P 500 fell 1.8% and US Technology fell 4.9%, while Health Care gained 0.45%. In Europe, AstraZeneca rose 7.0% and Sanofi 4.7% while the STOXX 600 fell 0.4%. Pictet links the rotation to investor selectivity on Technology's capital intensity and AI investment returns, not only to defensiveness.
GLP-1 pricing is a risk. Novo Nordisk plans to cut US list prices from January 2027.
US Health Care trades at 19.9x next-twelve-month earnings, up from 16.5x in April and above the ten-year average of 16.6x.
European Health Care trades at 16.3x next-twelve-month earnings, up from 14.8x at end-September and below the ten-year average of 17.2x. The discount to the broader market has narrowed to about 5.5%.

Earnings revision momentum is positive but has moderated in both regions. The European revision ratio fell to 14.4% at end-October from 24.0% at the start of the month. European rolling 12-month returns rose from 11% to 13%, below the 21% summer peak.

US Health Care is delivering 5.2% blended earnings growth and a 13.3% earnings surprise, the largest among S&P 500 sectors. 85% of reporters beat and 67% saw positive price reactions, against 60% for the S&P 500.
European Health Care is delivering 11.1% earnings growth and a 10.8% surprise. 73% of stocks reacted positively, against 54% for MSCI Europe.

Guidance is constructive across obesity, immunology and oncology. For 2027 and beyond, Pictet says performance depends more on launch execution, pricing and access, pipeline delivery and patent expiries.

Biotech could add a growth leg to the rotation, helped by improving financing conditions, renewed M&A and large pharma's need to replenish pipelines before patent expiries. XBI broke out above 140-143 and is testing its 50-day average near 152 with RSI near 48. 140-143 is key support.

US Health Care averaged 4.6% after 65 trading days, 9.8% after 125 days and 12.0% after 250 days following the five midterms since 1990 that left Democrats controlling at least one chamber. Pictet cautions the sample is small.
The SMI has substantial exposure to global pharma. It broke above 14,669, with the next technical objective near 15,200 and key support at 14,559-14,669.

sector_views.rationale: Pictet describes the backdrop as broadly constructive: improving relative momentum, strong earnings surprises and broad participation. It flags stretched RSI, valuation above the ten-year average and Lilly concentration as risks. The note does not state a formal rating.
Valuation is below the ten-year average and earnings growth is 11.1%, but revision momentum is fading. The note states no formal rating.
Financing, M&A and pipeline-replenishment tailwinds are supportive, but the technical picture is consolidation and the note calls the group typically more volatile.

earnings_insights: US Health Care Q3 season, as of 3 Nov 2026: blended earnings growth 5.2% and a 13.3% earnings surprise, the largest among S&P 500 sectors. 85% of reporters beat and 67% had positive price reactions (reported, season in progress).
European Health Care Q3 season, as of 3 Nov 2026: earnings growth 11.1% and a 10.8% surprise. 73% of stocks reacted positively (reported, season in progress).
Eli Lilly reported stronger-than-expected earnings and the stock gained about 11% over the week. The note gives no EPS figure.
European earnings revision ratio fell to 14.4% at end-October from 24.0% at the start of the month, an estimate-revision measure rather than a reported result.
Novo Nordisk plans to cut US list prices from January 2027 (company plan as cited by Pictet).
risk_factors: Concentration: Eli Lilly is about 16% of XLV, and the latest leg of the move is more concentrated than earlier gains.
GLP-1 pricing pressure, including Novo Nordisk's planned US list price cuts from January 2027.
Drugmakers' exposure to Medicare drug-pricing policy under a Democratic Congress.
US Health Care valuation of 19.9x forward earnings is above its ten-year average of 16.6x.
Earnings revision momentum has moderated in both the US and Europe.
The midterm-return sample is small (five episodes since 1990).
Launch execution, pricing and access, pipeline delivery and patent expiries drive 2027 performance.

tension_points.bull_case: Broad participation, a 13.3% earnings surprise, positive guidance across obesity, immunology and oncology, and a possible biotech growth leg support the rotation. The post-midterm history is positive.
tension_points.bear_case: US Health Care trades at 19.9x versus a 16.6x ten-year average. Lilly is about 16% of XLV, GLP-1 pricing is under pressure and revision momentum is moderating. The XLV/SPY RSI of 72.5 is stretched.
tension_points.what_invalidates: XLV/SPY falling back below the 0.2323 breakout area.

tension_points.bull_case: Less risk of further cuts to healthcare funding and coverage, which would support providers and areas exposed to coverage expansion.
tension_points.bear_case: Drugmakers remain exposed to Medicare drug-pricing policy, so the implications for them are less clear.

theme_stances.key_argument: Health Care combines a less cyclical earnings profile with improving growth and earnings momentum while investors grow more selective on Technology's AI capital intensity.
theme_stances.evidence: supported by earnings delivery, rather than defensiveness alone

theme_stances.key_argument: Improving financing, renewed M&A and pipeline-replenishment needs support interest in differentiated biotech assets.
A Democratic Congress could reduce the risk of further healthcare funding and coverage cuts, though drugmakers remain exposed to Medicare pricing.
